existing_not_reused.uc-clinical-20260930-reanalysis-4735-dat: Different cohorts (Talos study); no existing record describes the UKSH cohort, so three datasets were created.

existing_judgements_unchanged: All ten existing judgements on this use case are unchanged.

vocabulary_additions.note: No existing concept covers human hands-on review time (runtime is defined as computation time). Lower is better. No external match asserted. Needs review.

prose_values: All 27 results are printed in the article text (abstract and Results paragraphs). Each locator names the section, the paragraph number within it and the exact quoted phrase; the extractor asserts both. Figures, Table 1 (an image) and the supplement were not read.
per_patient_data: The supplement (352295_file02.xlsx, per-patient clinical data) was not downloaded. Case numbers, genes and variants printed in Results 'Manual Reanalysis' P1-P2 are not stored in any file.

judgements.endpoint: New P/LP and VUS case findings, case-category counts, manual review time and Talos candidates per case for manual and Talos reanalysis of the same 219 unresolved genomes
limitations: Unequal inputs: the manual arm re-aligned and re-called the raw reads with DRAGEN v4.2.4 and used Emedgene; Talos used the archived DRAGEN v3.7.5 VCFs. Differences cannot be attributed to the method alone.
The reference is the manual arm's own result: Talos is scored on whether it returned what manual reanalysis found, so findings that only Talos might have made are not counted.
Very small numbers: three new P/LP cases in each arm.

Automated total diagnostic yield is printed as 41.9% (Results 'Reanalysis Diagnostic Yield: Automated Reanalysis' P1), but 161 of 377 is 42.7%, which the manual paragraph and Figure 4 legend print; 41.9% is the initial yield.
Talos output per case is printed as an average of three variants (Results; Discussion P3) and as a median of approximately three (Discussion P1).
Manual time excludes report writing and preparation of evidence for secondary review; no hands-on time is printed for Talos.
Single centre, high initial yield (41.9%), one reanalysis round after a mean of 660 days.
A new candidate or classification is not a confirmed diagnosis; per-case confirmation details are in the supplement, which was not read.

judgements.endpoint: Share of 35 known P/LP variants and count of 21 known VUS that Talos prioritised in 45 singleton cases, with failure modes
limitations: Positive controls are known findings from the initial analysis; recovering them does not establish new diagnostic yield.
Concordance is per variant against the initial report, not per case.
The pipeline conversion share for singletons is 8.6% in the text but 9.6% in the Figure 2 legend; the text value is stored (3 of 35 is 8.6%).

judgements.endpoint: Share of 145 known P/LP variants Talos prioritised in 162 trio cases in trio mode and proband-only mode, VUS captured and failure modes
limitations: Positive controls are known findings from the initial analysis; recovering them does not establish new diagnostic yield.
Concordance is per variant against the initial report, not per case.
Strict inheritance filtering in trio mode excluded 11 P/LP variants that proband-only mode recovered.

relevance_decision: The reanalysis comparison is judged direct: same 219 unresolved cases, same interval, both arms with updated knowledge, case-level new findings and review effort for each arm. The arms did not get the same variant calls (manual re-called with DRAGEN v4.2.4; Talos used archived DRAGEN v3.7.5 VCFs), which favours the manual arm and means differences cannot be credited to the method alone; this is the first constraint a reader sees in the limitations. The two Talos benchmarking protocols are proxy because they rerank known findings.

evidence_gaps_add: The only same-cohort manual versus automated comparison found (Kaschta et al. 2026) gave the arms different variant calls and uses the manual result as the reference; no equal-input comparison exists in the store.
No hands-on time is printed for the automated arm; workload is printed as 81 minutes per manual case versus about three Talos variants per case, which are not the same unit.
Kaschta et al. 2026 is a single-centre preprint with three new P/LP cases per arm.

summary_proposal: Kaschta et al. (2026, preprint) reanalysed the same 219 genomes that had no P/LP finding after a mean of 660 days, once manually by the diagnostic laboratory and once with Talos 8.2.0. Manual reanalysis found three new P/LP cases and two new VUS cases, taking a mean of 81 minutes per case (Results). Talos also returned the three new P/LP cases and one of the two new VUS cases, with an average of three variants returned per case. The arms did not have the same inputs: the manual arm re-called the reads with a newer DRAGEN version, while Talos used the archived calls, and the manual result is also the reference. On known findings, Talos prioritised 80.0% of 35 P/LP variants in singletons and 75.2% of 145 in trios, rising to 82.8% in proband-only mode. The paper prints the automated total yield as 41.9%, although 161 of 377 cases is 42.7%. Values are transcribed from the article text, not reproduced, and do not establish confirmed diagnoses. This summary describes evidence and does not recommend a workflow.
